title: Complete and incomplete combustion comparison sheet
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 12 (Complete and incomplete combustion comparison sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 12: Incomplete combustion and carbon monoxide. To understand why incomplete combustion happens and why its products are harmful

model.title: Write word equations for methane burning completely and incompletely

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Complete: methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Incomplete: methane + oxygen → carbon monoxide + water

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Very little oxygen: carbon (soot) can form instead

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: Products depend on the oxygen supply

questions.q: Write a word equation for methane burning with very little oxygen.
questions.a: methane + oxygen → carbon monoxide + water (or carbon + water)
questions.model: Limited oxygen means the carbon cannot become carbon dioxide. It becomes carbon monoxide (or carbon). Hydrogen still becomes water. So methane + oxygen → carbon monoxide + water.

questions.q: What colour flame shows incomplete combustion?
Why does incomplete combustion release less energy?
questions.a: The fuel is not fully oxidised.

questions.q: Core: Make a comparison table of complete and incomplete combustion (oxygen, flame, products, energy, dangers).
questions.a: Complete: plenty of oxygen, blue, CO₂ + H₂O, more energy; incomplete: limited oxygen, yellow, CO, C, H₂O, less energy, poisonous.
questions.model: Teacher fills the first row: oxygen supply: plenty (complete) or limited (incomplete).

questions.q: Extend: Explain how carbon monoxide stops the blood carrying oxygen. Write in the portal response box.
questions.a: CO binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells, so less oxygen can be carried to the body's cells.

questions.q: Stretch: Why are CO alarms recommended near gas boilers?
questions.a: A faulty boiler with poor air supply can burn incompletely and release CO, which cannot be detected by our senses.

questions.q: Which gas is made only in incomplete combustion?
Big question: why is a yellow, smoky flame more dangerous than a blue one?
questions.a: It shows incomplete combustion, which makes poisonous carbon monoxide and soot.
